key_insight: Accounting for temperature-dependent water properties through corrected integral profile transformations predicts turbulent friction and heat transfer within 2% of DNS, except at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: Property-aware predictions can improve water-channel thermal design where constant-property assumptions and empirical correlations misestimate friction and heat transfer.
method: Run plane-channel DNS of heated and cooled water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity.
Derive mean-profile transformations from momentum and energy balances, calibrating turbulent transport corrections against DNS.
Apply the corrections to the Spalart–Allmaras turbulence model.
evidence_signal: Across wall temperatures of 277–360 K and wall Prandtl numbers of 2–12, DNS shows friction changes of −39% to +32% versus constant-property flow and empirical-correlation errors up to 26%.
watch_item: The corrections are DNS-calibrated for constant-density plane-channel flow, and transformation accuracy deteriorates at the lowest Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Direct numerical simulation of turbulent heat transfer in water with temperature-dependent viscosity and conductivity
